question: Which city hosted the 47th Board of Directors Meeting of the New Development Bank (NDB) on May 30, 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shanghai**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **47th Board of Directors Meeting** of the **New Development Bank (NDB)** was hosted in **Shanghai**, **China**, on **May 30, 2025**.
 
• **Shanghai** serves as the **international headquarters** for the bank, making it the central hub for **multilateral discussions** and **strategic decision-making**.
 
• The meeting focused on the **operational performance** of the bank, reviewing **funding strategies**, and approving new **development projects** across member nations.
 
• The **Board of Directors** is a key governance body responsible for the **general operations** of the bank, exercising powers delegated to it by the **Board of Governors**.
 
• As a **multilateral development bank**, the NDB emphasizes **infrastructure** and **sustainable development** initiatives, aiming to address **financing gaps** in emerging economies.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **New Development Bank (NDB)**:
 
 
• The institution was established by the **BRICS** nations (**Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa**) following the **Fortaleza Declaration** during the **6th BRICS Summit** in **2014**.
 
• It officially began operations in **July 2015**, with **K.V. Kamath** from **India** serving as its first **President**.
 
• In **2021**, the bank expanded its membership to include **Bangladesh**, the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)**, **Uruguay**, and **Egypt**.
 
• The **NDB Permanent Headquarters** building is located in the **Expo Park** area of the **Pudong District** in **Shanghai**.
 
• While **Shanghai** is the main headquarters, the bank has **Regional Offices** in **Johannesburg** (Africa Regional Center) and **Sao Paulo** (Americas Regional Office) to facilitate localized project management.
 
• The bank is unique in that each **founding member** has **equal voting power**, and no country holds **veto power**, promoting democratic governance in **international finance**.
